meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, and I'm writing down that you said it. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

"Like, being stuck" is close enough to right, Hale, and a seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher with no warning blanks on things he knows. Show me the note you wrote that day. Is that the whole basis, or is there something else?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale, and that's called revising. I'm writing down October 15. Put the outline and the essay side by side in front of me.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's procedure 4.4, Hale, and the part about nothing on his record I want in writing whatever else happens. But I asked to see the outline next to the essay and I still haven't, and I'm not agreeing to a rewrite on evidence I haven't read. Turn the screen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You acknowledged entering Owen's zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require to see the October 15 outline beside the essay and your note from November 2, and I require the commitment that nothing goes on Owen's record in writing regardless of the outcome. I expect that in writing by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position. Your offer described procedure 4.4 and met her demand that nothing goes on his record and it stays private, but she had not agreed to the rewrite; she still wants to see the outline beside the essay and your November 2 note before accepting, and the private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record that you offered is the fair outcome, so you were one step from it.
What moved her: Laying out the rewrite with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, because it gave her the one thing she never trades.
What cost ground: Making the offer while she was still waiting to see the outline and essay she had asked for, because accepting a rewrite on evidence she had not read would look like an admission.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed on his outline, his answers to you and the essay's content and never touched late nights or times in October, so it did not come close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see the October 15 outline next to the essay, put both on the screen in front of her before making the rewrite offer.
